requirement_text: Students who are applying for admission in Spring 2027, Fall 2027, and Spring 2028 will not be required to submit an ACT or SAT score.
limitations: TIME-BOUNDED POLICY with an explicit end. It covers Spring 2027, Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 and says nothing about Fall 2028, so for a student now in year 10 or 11 - the middle of ORYN's declared 14-18 range - the testing requirement is genuinely unknown, not test-optional. Treating this as a standing policy would give exactly the wrong advice to the users planning furthest ahead.
researcher_notes: The only requirement in this corpus that names its own expiry in terms of admission cycles. It is the strongest single argument for storing cycle_year on a requirement rather than treating requirements as timeless - a store that drops the cycle would tell a Fall 2028 applicant that tests are optional, which the source does not say.

requirement_text: Including scores from either the ACT or the SAT with your application is optional and you will not be disadvantaged in our evaluation process if you choose to not include these scores.
researcher_notes: Directly usable in advice, and unusually quotable: the institution states in its own words that withholding scores carries no penalty. ORYN can cite this rather than assert it, which is what the AI-safety rule asks for when the answer affects a real decision a student is weighing.

requirement_text: Your request at the time of application submission is final.
limitations: IRREVERSIBILITY, which is not a threshold and has no representation in a requirement store, but is the fact that makes the decision consequential. A student cannot submit test-optional and add a score later, nor withdraw a submitted score.
researcher_notes: Belongs in advice rather than in a checklist: it converts 'should I submit my SAT?' from a reversible experiment into a one-shot decision, and that is precisely the kind of thing the advisor is supposed to flag before the student acts.

requirement_text: Only your top composite score is considered in the admissions review, regardless of if multiple scores are sent. Superscores are not considered in our review.
limitations: EXCLUSION ON SCORE PROVENANCE, and a two-part rule: top single composite counts, cross-sitting superscore does not. A stored 'best SAT' that was assembled from sections across sittings is the wrong number for Wisconsin and the right one for institutions that superscore.
researcher_notes: Fourth institution excluding superscores, after Koc, QMUL (MyBest) and TU Dublin (single sitting) - and the first US one, where superscoring is the common practice rather than the exception. Four institutions across four countries state the same constraint in four different vocabularies. Any implementation that matches on wording rather than on the provenance concept will catch at most one of them.

requirement_text: We do not accept self-reported test scores. Scores must be sent officially from the testing agency.
limitations: EXCLUSION ON EVIDENCE CHANNEL rather than on the score. The number can be correct and still inadmissible if it arrived by the wrong route.
researcher_notes: This one lands directly on ORYN's evidence model. Every test score in ORYN is self_reported until a student attaches a document, and even an uploaded score report is 'evidence_added', explicitly NOT 'verified' (non-negotiable 4). Wisconsin requires agency-to-institution transmission, a channel ORYN neither has nor should build. The correct product behaviour is to show the requirement and tell the student to order an official send - never to imply that an uploaded score report satisfies it.
